sources.title: Three inspected NPS first-flight accounts: original reading notes
sources.provenance: Three official National Park Service pages, inspected 2026-10-20; URLs and limitations in the notes. Institutional retrospective accounts, not independent primary witnesses.
sources.locator_scheme: Numbered units 1–3; the complete agreed source scope is these three historical accounts, not the full Wright biography.

rights.basis: Historical facts paraphrased in original notes and original dramatic writing; no copied passages, images or archival texts. No legal certification of underlying third-party contributions.

contract.scope: A complete compact historical short about measurement and the end of the flying day, not a feature or biography. Demonstration author approved these choices; no user interview is represented.
preserve: Date, place, first and fourth flight measurements, alternating pilots, four flights, wind damage, later telegram to father.
contract.change_policy: Original private conversation and gestures; compress middle flights; invent notebook scene as an explicitly reconstructed dramatic device. Never quote an uninspected telegram.

departures.description: All spoken dialogue, pocket screw, notebook handling and final message composition are invented.
departures.reason: Turn measurements and an event sequence into visible choices and a restrained relationship; no claim of verbatim history.

departures.description: Middle two flights compressed into a montage; location of final writing invented.
departures.reason: Keep a compact short focused on testing, measurement and preserving a record.

scenes.transformation: Invent a practical repair exchange to externalize care without a speech about brotherhood.
Show launch, camera and landing through action; dialogue after landing is invented.
Turn flight measurements into a physical measuring task.
Compress two flights and show alternating responsibility; preserve four total.
Show established wind damage; private repair exchange and notebook details are invented.
Invent a restrained writing scene; keep telegram wording out of view.
